newsitem.title: USA: PG&E convicted of causing 1994 Calif. fire.
newsitem.headline: PG&E convicted of causing 1994 Calif. fire.

text.p: Pacific Gas & Electric Co., a unit of PG&E Corp., was convicted on Thursday of causing a 1994 northern California forest fire by neglecting to trim trees, one of which touched a high-voltage power line to ignite the blaze.
A jury in Nevada County Municipal Court also found the utility guilty on all but four of 742 other misdemeanor counts involving trimming trees around power lines.
PG&E could face up to $2 million in fines and assessments.
The jury of six men and six women deliberated for 20 hours at the end of the 32-day trial before reaching its verdict. It took 50 minutes to read the hundreds of counts.
It was the first time PG&E had been criminally prosecuted in California for neglecting to trim trees and the trial was closely watched by other counties.
The giant utility was found guilty of causing the Aug. 7, 1994 Trauner fire which burned 500 acres, destroyed 12 buildings and caused $3 million in damage.

PG&E immediately filed a motion for a new trial. Judge Carlos Baker will hear legal arguments on the motion on July 2. If the motion is denied, sentencing could be the same day. PG&E has not yet said if it will appeal.
Bill Roake, a spokesman for PG&E, said the utility remains "supremely confident our tree-trimming programme is one of the premiere programmes in the U.S."
The utility trims about 5,000 trees a day within its northern and central California service territory, he noted.
Given the scale of the efforts, he conceded future accidents could not be ruled out.
Roake said he believed this was the only time the utility has been charged with tree-trimming failure.
But the Nevada City jury found PG&E guilty of deliberately limiting its tree maintenance programme, violating a series of state laws on power line clearance and fire breaks.
